authoritative_command: Application service receives an already transport-validated command.
A unit-of-work obtains an authoritative connection from the owned connection factory.
The connection proves required SQLite enforcement before the transaction begins.
Required authoritative state is loaded and the owning domain policy revalidates the command against the current revision/state.
Structural constraints and domain mutation are applied inside the bounded transaction.
Required domain-event/audit persistence participates in the same commit boundary according to HLD-14.
Commit publishes the complete accepted result; failure rolls the unit back and returns a stable failure category.
long_running_or_external_work: Adapter/job captures the minimum authoritative revision/input identities needed for work.
The transaction is released before workbook/mail/file parsing, expensive computation, waiting, or operator review.
Intermediate restart-safe job/proposal/checkpoint state is persisted separately when required.
Before authoritative mutation, a fresh short transaction reloads the target and revalidates stale/conflict conditions.
Only the accepted minimal result is committed; source content itself does not remain an open database transaction.
startup_migration: HLD-01 host acquires canonical data-instance ownership.
Migration coordinator obtains exclusive migrator authority and rereads package manifest, database ledger, and schema.
Unknown/missing/drifted/future/invalid states are classified before mutation.
Each required accepted migration applies schema/data change and migration-ledger evidence atomically.
On any failure the database remains at the last committed migration state.
Post-migration exact-schema, foreign-key and required append-only/integrity checks execute.
Only a passing current state returns persistence readiness to HLD-01.
observational_status: Status determines whether the target exists without creating it.
Existing targets are opened through explicit read-only/query-only semantics when safe.
Manifest/ledger/schema/integrity state is classified without migration, repair, checkpoint, vacuum, write pragma, timestamp touch, lock disruption, or default creation.

If a live verified SOMA host owns the database, detailed live status is requested through that host where required; unsafe offline inspection reports limited/unavailable instead of disturbing the writer.
typed_json_write: Owning capability selects an explicit named/versioned JSON contract.
Input is parsed with strict duplicate/nonfinite/malformed rejection and validated for shape, semantics, bounds, and version.
Unknown fields/versions follow the explicit contract policy; no silent loss is followed by overwrite.
Upgrade or normal write commits atomically and failure preserves the prior valid document.
projection_rebuild: Projection/cache state is treated as disposable and non-authoritative.
Owning canonical relational facts/events are read from SQLite.
Projection is deterministically regenerated and may be replaced without altering canonical lifecycle/audit evidence.
A projection that cannot be rebuilt from accepted authority is not permitted as a cache and must be modeled as authoritative domain data instead.
restore_publication: HLD-13 authenticates/decrypts and prepares a candidate restore without replacing the live instance prematurely.
HLD-02 validates that the candidate is a supported database with coherent migration lineage, exact schema expectations, foreign keys, and required integrity/append-only protections.
Only a verified candidate may be atomically published as the restored data instance under HLD-13 recovery rules.
Failure leaves the prior valid instance unchanged.

performance_rules: Keep write transactions bounded to authoritative validation/mutation, never operator think-time or source parsing.
Index every effective child-side FK path used by ordinary joins or parent integrity checks unless a documented measured exception exists.
Prefer relational queries over denormalized duplicate truth; add rebuildable projections only for measured query needs.
Batch operations preflight outside the write transaction where possible, then revalidate/commit bounded deterministic partitions according to owning-domain atomicity.
